A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PAVA and restarted-FISTA approach to certifying sparse GLMs. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 and Appendix C report original runtime, convergence, GPU-acceleration, and optimality-certification experiments on synthetic and real-world data.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments, revises the DOROTHEA results, and adds large-k runtime results and numerical comparisons of perspective and ℓ1 relaxations.

M1.justification: V2 corrects the printed procedures: Algorithm 2 returns half the sum of squared majorization coefficients, and Algorithm 3 uses the resettable momentum counter φ/(φ+3) instead of t/(t+3). The core method remains intact; these corrections do not establish that the implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic linear/logistic regression, Cancer Drug Response, and DOROTHEA. Resampling and larger k change settings within this coverage. The added multinomial-logistic formula is not accompanied by an evaluated multiclass task.

E2.justification: Appendix C.2 adds an evaluated ℓ1-relaxation comparator following Mhenni et al. (2020), with results in Tables 3–4. The existing commercial/open-source solver comparisons and PGD/FISTA convergence comparators are retained.

E3.justification: The real-data protocol changes substantially: Appendix B.3 replaces arbitrary k selection with five-fold cross-validation and introduces balanced DOROTHEA resampling. Table 2 changes its setting from n=1150, p=91598, k=15 to n=2300, p=89989, k=10; v1's appendix inconsistently states n=1950. New experiments test k=500 and compare relaxation objective values. The reported GPU also changes from RTX A5000 to A100, without establishing a rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix C.1.4 adds a large-k sensitivity test at k=500, extending the existing parameter studies. Appendix C.2 adds an analysis of bound tightness for perspective versus ℓ1 relaxation. Existing restart and parameter-sensitivity analyses remain.

E5.justification: Appendices B.1–B.2 retain five repetitions with different random seeds and mean/standard-deviation reporting. No changed run counts, new uncertainty-estimation procedures, or significance tests are stated. The new cross-validation procedure concerns hyperparameter selection.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces DOROTHEA results: the proposed method changes from 91 seconds/0% gap to 230 seconds/0%; MOSEK changes from 634 seconds/0% to 1814 seconds/0.63%, under different settings. Table 1 and other Table 2 rows are unchanged. Figure 13 adds large-k timings; Tables 3–4 add higher perspective-relaxation bounds than ℓ1 across the reported dimensions.

T1.justification: V2 restores a missing summation in the conjugate derivation and explicitly accounts for sorting in Theorem 3.2's complexity proof. It also adds the ℓ1-relaxation formulation and a multinomial-logistic loss/conjugate pair. The central lemmas, theorems, and proof framework are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same principal claims: exact log-linear proximal evaluation, accelerated lower-bound computation through restarted FISTA and GPUs, and substantial optimality-certification speedups.

C2.justification: V2 explains why smoothing TopSum could compromise certification, motivates small k through prediction and overfitting considerations, and discusses the tightness/computational-cost tradeoff against stronger rank-one SOCP and SDP relaxations. These extend the interpretation of the retained approach.

D1.justification: V2 adds an OKGLM code-access statement, documents DOROTHEA resampling and cross-validation selection, and identifies the Delta/ACCESS computing environment. Appendix B.4 changes the GPU specification from RTX A5000 to A100 while Table 1's timings remain identical.

R1.justification: V2 positions the finite-M method relative to earlier k-support-norm proximal algorithms by Argyriou et al. and McDonald et al. It also adds discussion and citations concerning ℓ1 relaxations, smooth top-k approximations, perspective formulations, and GPU heuristics.

P1.justification: The section sequence and most prose remain stable. V2 edits introductory wording, expands selected explanations, adds appendix subsections and code/acknowledgment/impact statements, and updates publication information. This is localized revision rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: V2 replaces raster plots with vector graphics and adjusts typography, spacing, captions, and appendix placement. It adds Figure 13 and Tables 3–4. Existing plot organizations and main-table structures are largely preserved.

improvement.justification: V2 improves the written algorithm through the value-evaluation and restart corrections, adds useful large-k and relaxation-tightness evidence, and clarifies prior-work relationships and reproducibility information. These strengthen an otherwise retained study. The changed DOROTHEA settings limit direct cross-version timing comparisons, so its replacement results do not establish a performance improvement over v1.
